newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks seen in holding pattern.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen in holding pattern.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are seen moving in a broad range with a slight downward bias in the coming week, but an expected decline in trading activity and turnover should limit any downward momentum, brokers said.
"I am wary of being too bearish at this time," said David Robinson, regional investment strategist at HSBC James Capel.
"But I also think there will be a chance to buy blue chips at lower prices in a few, say four, weeks."
The Hang Seng Index closed 24.95 points higher at 12,541.18 on turnover of HK$6.88 billion ($890 million) on Friday.

Activity was centred on a handful of blue chips and a wide range of red chip China plays and second line issues. Over the week, the index added just 24.58 points, or 0.20 percent. Red chips are Hong Kong companies with strong China ties.
"We are recommending investors accumulate on weakness," said Robinson.
Key U.S. economic data due in the coming week was clouding the outlook for U.S. stocks and bonds, and added to analysts' cautious view of the domestic market.

The Dow industrials rose 44.95 points or 0.68 percent to close at 6,703.55 on Friday after a choppy trading session. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond closed 4/32 higher at 94-21/32 to yield 7.06 percent compared with its 7.07 percent close on Thursday.
"Consumer confidence reports and the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) report due out in the following week could knock complacency out of the (U.S.) bond market," said Robinson.
The U.S. data could point to a stronger U.S. economy and the need for another inflation-curbing interest rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve Board at the end of May, he said.

On Friday, U.S. market sources said the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for April came in equal to the index's all-time high of 101.0 set in March 1984, indicating that robust consumer spending was likely to fuel growth.
The University of Michigan, which releases its index only to subscribers, declined to comment on the data.
"The market has a positive tone but I really don't see it doing too much in the next week," Franco Tong in institutional sales at New China Hong Kong, said of the local market.
Some brokers said the Hang Seng index would start the week on a firm note but succumb to pressure from the expiry of derivatives contracts at the end of the week.
"The index should basically trade within a 200-point band. There could be a little weakness toward the end of the week," said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
The last day for trading in the April index futures contract will be Tuesday, April 29, but position squaring was likely ahead of the expiry, Delgado said.
Charts show the Hang Seng index faces short-term resistance at the 12,600 level, analysts said.
"If the index does manage to break that level, there is more resistance at 13,000. We are likely to trade in the 12,000 to 13,000 range," said Delgado.
Property counters could show some strength, but trading in blue chips will take a back seat to red chips, said New China's Tong.
Red chip Tian An China Investments Co Ltd will report its 1996 final results on Monday and will put the spotlight back on the outlook for China property plays.
H-share Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd will also report 1996 results on Monday, and Guangshen Railway Co Ltd will report on Wednesday. Tsingtao Brewery will report its results on Thursday.
H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares of large China-incorporated enterprises.
